title: Keycap Forge
pitch: **Design printable custom keycaps with ChatGPT, WebMCP, and browser-local 3D AI.**
about_excerpt: **Design printable custom keycaps with ChatGPT, WebMCP, and browser-local 3D AI.** Like Comment Story Updates Inspiration Creating an artisan keycap usually requires several disconnected skills: generating a concept, modeling it in Blender or CAD, understanding keycap dimensions, building a switch-compatible mount, repairing the mesh, and preparing it for 3D printing. At the same time, most image-to-3D demonstrations stop after producing something visually interesting. They rarely answer the practical question: Can this model be edited, attached to a real keycap, validated, and printed? We also wanted to explore a better way for ChatGPT to interact with complex web applications. Traditional browser agents depend on coordinates and simulated clicks, which become fragile when layouts change. WebMCP offered a different approach: the website could expose meaningful tools such as find_parts , auto_place_part , and compose_keycap . That led to Keycap Forge: a browser-based workspace where a person and ChatGPT can collaboratively turn an image into a printable custom keycap. What it does Keycap Forge is a browser-local 3D keycap editor powered by WebMCP. A user can: Choose a standard key size, from 1U through 6.25U Space . Select an MX or Topre switch mount. Generate a standalone 3D statue from a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG reference image. Create a lightweight 2.5D relief from a logo or silhouette. Import an existing watertight STL model. Select, move, rotate, and scale parts directly in the 3D viewport. Automatically center and fit a model on the keycap. Render the keycap and added model as one manufacturing solid. Inspect solid, section, and underside views. Validate manifold connectivity, volume, and dimensions. Return to the editable state without losing the original parts or transforms. Export an STL only after explicit user approval. Download a tolerance coupon before printing the complete keycap. The same project can also be controlled conversationally through ChatGPT. Keycap Forge exposes semantic WebMCP tools including: describe_project find_parts get_project_state transform_part auto_place_part compose_keycap repair_printability set_keycap_spec undo_last_action validate_printability export_project Instead of asking ChatGPT to locate a colored arrow on the screen, the user can say: Find the cat model, center it on the keycap, enlarge it slightly, and validate the result. ChatGPT can then operate on the actual project state while every change remains visible and reversible in the website. How we built it The editor is built with React, TypeScript, vinext, and Vite. Three.js and React Three Fiber power the interactive 3D viewport. The keycap itself is generated from deterministic manufacturing parameters rather than being a decorative cube. The geometry includes: A flat-top tapered shell Rounded corners An underside cavity MX cross or Topre mount geometry Stabilizer stems for supported wide MX keys Millimeter-based positioning and tolerances For photo-to-3D generation, we run a browser-compatible TripoSR ONNX pipeline using ONNX Runtime WebGPU. The uploaded image stays on the user’s device. The reconstruction pipeline: Removes a connected edge background and centers the subject. Converts the image into a 512 × 512 model tensor. Runs the TripoSR encoder, backbone, and decoder through WebGPU. Evaluates a (192^3) density field. Smooths the level set to reduce voxel noise. Extracts a surface using marching cubes. Welds duplicate vertices. Applies Taubin smoothing to improve print quality without excessive shrinkage. Corrects the generated model’s up axis and front-facing direction. Normalizes the statue to a practical keycap scale. The three model files total approximately 801 MiB. To make that viable on a static deployment, we implemented parallel byte-range downloading, retries, and resumable chunk storage using the Origin Private File System. A refresh can reuse chunks that have already been downloaded. Manufacturing composition uses Manifold WASM. During Render union , Keycap Forge applies the latest part transforms, removes geometry extending into the keycap cavity, preserves a small attachment overlap, and combines everything into one solid. WebMCP is integrated through a typed tool registry. Zod validates every tool input, and state-changing calls include an expectedRevision . If ChatGPT tries to modify an outdated revision, the operation is rejected instead of overwriting a newer human edit. Manual UI operations and WebMCP operations share the same command and history system. This keeps agent actions observable, undoable, and consistent with direct editing. Challenges we ran into Turning one image into a useful 3D object A single image does not contain information about hidden surfaces. Early approaches produced flat extrusions rather than statue-like objects. TripoSR provided genuine single-view reconstruction, but its raw output still required orientation correction, surface smoothing, normalization, and manufacturing checks. Running a large model on a static deployment The first browser model download is approximately 801 MiB. A normal Vite deployment could host the interface, but unreliable downloads made the main feature unusable. We addressed this by splitting model files into resumable ranges, downloading multiple chunks concurrently, retrying failed ranges, and storing completed chunks in OPFS. Correcting model orientation The reconstruction coordinate system did not match the editor’s coordinate system. Models initially arrived lying down, upside down, or facing away from the camera. We mapped the TripoSR axes into the editor’s right-handed millimeter coordinate system and added a front-facing correction before placement. Separating camera movement from model manipulation The 3D viewport needed to support both orbit controls and transform gizmos. Pointer events originally reached the camera while the user was dragging a model handle. We had to coordinate selection, transform controls, and camera controls so that dragging a gizmo manipulates the part while dragging empty space rotates the camera. Preserving edits during Boolean composition An early union path regenerated parts from their initial state, which discarded the user’s latest rotation or scale. We changed the manufacturing pipeline to operate on a snapshot of the current project revision and apply every stored transform before the Boolean operation. Protecting the keycap cavity A model could look correctly placed from above while extending through the roof and blocking the switch cavity. The manufacturing pipeline now prioritizes the keycap base and trims added geometry below the roof, while retaining a small overlap for reliable attachment. Designing safe agent tools WebMCP gives an agent real application capabilities, so tool boundaries matter. We separated read-only inspection, reversible editing, validation, and consequential export. video_transcript_excerpt: Most AI agents control websites by guessing pixels. Keycap Forge gives ChatGPT a real modeling vocabulary. We start with a ChatGPT generated reference designed for reconstruction, a full-body cat three-quarter view, connected toy-like volumes, and no fragile fur or whiskers. Inside Keycap Forge, I create a one-unit keycap and upload that image. TripoSR runs WebGPU in the browser. The first run downloads the model once while the source image never leaves the device. Here, the weight is time-lapsed, but the result is real. 75,212 triangles corrected to stand upright and face forward, grounded on the roof, and normalized to an 8-mm printable statue. The website still works as a direct modeling tool. I can move, rotate, and scale the cat myself. Now, I deliberately leave it off-center with a rougher surface finish. This is where WebMCP changes the workflow. ChatGPT does not search for colored arrows or replay brittle clicks. The page exposes typed semantic tools over the live project. Find parts identifies the imported cat and reads its current transform. Repair printability previews both the unsafe placement and surface change before anything is applied. Autoplace parts centers the cat on the roof using the keycap's actual dimensions. After that preview, repair printability applies print smooth. Compose keycap batches the final 10-degree rotation and a larger, balanced scale into the same revision history. Every agent action appears immediately in the website. The user can inspect the result, undo it, or return to manual editing. Render union builds the manufacturing solid. Validate printability confirms one watertight component and its exact bounds. Export project opens an approval dialogue instead of downloading silently. Only the user releases the final STL. Keycap Forge turns browser-local 3D reconstruction and CAD-like editing into a visible, reversible collaboration between ChatGPT and a real web application without a paid 3D generation API.

live_observation.first_impression: A focused “Forge a printable keycap” start screen offers keycap size choices and a New keycap action.
live_observation.after_state: The editor opened with a flat-top 1u base, canvas, transform controls, STL/photo/logo upload options, socket and size choices, and a printable baseline download.
live_observation.notes: The central editor workflow is directly usable without login; AI photo upload requires a file and was not attempted.
